resources.string: Reads the on screen text only to find cookie and tracking consent prompts, then taps the reject option or switches optional choices off. It does not send anything anywhere and keeps nothing except your settings. It works on a best effort basis and can miss things.

ConsentGuard works on a best effort basis. It tries to reject cookie and tracking choices and to switch off optional ones, but it can miss some, and it cannot promise that a site stops tracking you or that any law is met. Choices a site marks as required or essential are left on. If it is not sure that every optional switch is off, it does not press Save or Confirm and leaves the panel as it is. Check the sites that matter to you yourself.

Banking and payment apps are never monitored. ConsentGuard checks the app name first and stops before it reads anything on the screen. Email and chat apps are left alone too. If an app is missing from the list, add it below.

No internet access: Android only allows an app to use the network if its manifest declares the INTERNET permission. ConsentGuard does not ask for this permission. You can independently verify this: in Android settings, the app's data usage stays at 0.

In a browser it must read the page to find a cookie banner, and it does nothing on screens that look like payment or sign in forms.

Banking and payment apps are never monitored by ConsentGuard. It checks the app name first and does not read their screens. Tap Apps to skip to see the list on your phone. It also has no internet permission, so it cannot send anything off your phone.
